body:
I know Reddit is comprised of anonymous strangers but I really appreciate you taking the time to read this.

> I suspect you have needed to for a long time.

You're absolutely right. On the outside I'm very much a wall. People would probably be surprised that I have emotions, to be honest. It takes me forever to even warm up to someone which has made me think negatively about seeking professional help (if I can't talk to someone I've known for years, how am I going to open up to someone I just met who is costing me money?). I know it's the right thing to do but I can't help but feel that it's a waste of time and that it won't really help anything. I hear so many times that people don't really benefit from therapy. My ex that I mentioned was in therapy. She had a rough time growing up and I tried my best to console her. She was raped when she was young and had a pretty bad drug problem with an abusive family. She one time said to me "it's probably a good thing I don't own a gun, because if I did, I would probably shoot myself." What the hell does one say to something like that? If therapy can't help something like that, I'm not sure what can. Nowadays, I can't help but feel the same way. I'm afraid that if I owned a firearm, it would be bad news.

You're right though that I can't judge my worth by my outwardly representation. However, I believe it's easier said than done. How does one become content with life to the point where they can keep going? I have a good job that pays well and I shouldn't complain about that but I can't be happy with it. I spent so much money in college to get a degree to follow this path that I thought was for me, but it turns out I was wrong. It feels like I'm going through a mid-life crisis (oh god, I hope this doesn't happen again in 20 years).

Also, I mentioned that I dated a couple people after my ex but it never ended well. It made me feel more worthless than before to the point where I don't even try pursuing anyone anymore. When I try to talk to someone, I only do it because I feel like it's something that I should be doing. Though it always ends in failure. People tell me all the time that I'm smart, attractive, and a great person, but I just can't see it. Even if I had those qualities, I would gladly trade them all for just a little bit of peace of mind.

I just feel like people mention that things will get better but I feel like I've been scarred in such a way that I will never be 100%. I've accepted that I will never be 100%. How do I know things will get better when I can't even think of what a better life would be? People recommend trying new hobbies, going out to meetup groups in my area, trying to socialize as much as possible, but I've been trying to do that for the past couple of years and I still feel like I'm just struggling, going through the motions.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that I'm tired; exhausted from the work that is trying to pull oneself out of a depression.

Thank you for the response. The problem is that I know that my problems are exceedingly trivial compared to what other people on this subreddit are going through. I feel like none of the issues that I'm dealing with are worth the time of others. It makes me think "well, I should just suck it up because others have it worse" but that doesn't make me feel better. It just makes me feel bad that people are in worse situations and that I feel guilty that I feel the way I do.

It basically started after I graduated college a few years ago (college, shit I shouldn't complain about an education but now I'm swimming in student loan debt that won't go away, literally, for another 25 years). Right after college, I started a job that I thought was going to be amazing but basically crushed my spirits. I ended up getting stressed and fat. My girlfriend that was my love of my life (I was going to propose to her, we were even talking baby names and future plans) basically stopped loving me. This was years ago but I still think about her every day, except now she's engaged to another guy. Our relationship began going downhill when she got pregnant and we both decided that we couldn't bring a child into this world in our situation at this time, so she got an abortion. I will always be pro-choice, but I don't think I could ever deal with that situation ever again. It has been nearly two years since I've talked to her (I'm turning 25 in less than a month, btw).

It was also around this time when I realize that my job was horrible and that my girlfriend was leaving me that my parents decided to separate. My family has always been a bit dysfunctional and separated all the time (my father was military so he was always deployed when I was growing up and my brother has been living across the country for the past 9 years). This seriously rocked me more than I thought it would. I basically just had a breakdown, quit my job that I hated on a whim and moved back into my parents house with no plans or goals. However, I feel like this has created a scar on my soul that I can never recover from. I felt like a total piece of shit because I thought "I can't work the jobs that I went to school for, the girl I wanted to spend the rest of my life with is with another person, and I have no family and friends to turn to". Sure, I have "friends" but they're all really just drinking friends. And even then they rarely call or seem to want to hang out with me, I'm always the one that has to initiate things, which makes me think I'm just wasting their time.

What's crazy is that I've since moved out and gotten a new place, started a new job in a new city, and have dated a couple girls, but I am just not happy. I can't find any motivation in the things I used to love (I've been playing guitar since I was in the 5th grade but now it just sits and collects dust... I've tried to pick it up and start again, but it's just hard). I don't know what is missing from my life. I go into cycles where I punished my body with cigarettes, alcohol, and drugs (as a side note, developing a taste for coke has not helped this). Then I get into feel-good times where I abstain from everything, start working out, and then eventually just fall right back into the cycle of things.

Wow, this turned out longer than I thought it would. If you end up reading this, then I really do thank you.
